To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a cadherin‐ like protein functions as a major binding site for Bacillus thurigiensis Cry1Aa or Cry1Ac toxin in the midguts of silkworms.
a cadherin‐type receptor protein functions as a major Cry1Aa receptor on B. mori MECs.
BtR1, a cadherin‐related protein, functions as a receptor on B. mori MECs and that APN does not play a major role in Cry1A toxin‐induced lyses of these cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of APN in Cry1A toxin‐mediated toxicity.
the identification and characterization of the receptor proteins for Cry1Aa, Cry1Ac, and Cry2Aa toxins on MECs of B. morl larvae.
the identification of BtR175 as a major receptor of Cry1A toxins on the surface of MECs in B. mori.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cadherin‐related proteins are the receptors for Cry1Aa, Cry1Ac, and Cry1Fa toxins, whereas aminopeptidases are the receptors for all Cry1Ab toxins.
Cry1Aa or Cry1Ac binds to APN and BtR1, but only the latter mediates the toxic effects.
the Cry1Ac and Cry1Aa toxins are able to interact with the B. mori cadherin protein, BtR175, on the surface of MECs, which is the first step in their mechanism of action.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the B. thuringiensis toxin Cry1Aa binds to a cadherin‐type receptor on the brush border membranes of the midguts of B. moris larvae and that the receptor is a 175‐kDa protein (Bt175).

the Cry1Aa or Cry1Ac toxin binds to BtR175, which is present on the microvillus membrane of the columnar cells, and the receptor–toxin complex is internalized by endocytosis, which is a process that is inhibited by anti‐Bt R175 antibody.
BtR1 is a receptor of the Cry1A toxins and BtR2 is a receptor of Cry1C toxin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cadherin‐type protein is a major receptor for the Cry1A toxins.
Cry toxins bind to cadherin‐related proteins on the microvillus membrane, but not on the lateral cell membrane that makes cell‐cell contacts.
the B. mori cadherin‐related protein, BtR175, acts as the major receptor for Cry toxins.
